Violation ID: 8240288
Permit API: 053-30507
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Harmony Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/07/2025
Comments: At a tank battery located approx 260' SW from the Cornplanter C well, DCNR staff notified the Department there was a release at this tank farm on July 3 2025. I contacted the operator of the well (Joe Thompson) Devonian Resources and Joe quickly dispatched a clean up crew and had the impacted soil removed later that afternoon. The discharge occurred from a tanker truck that was hauling a load of oil from the tank battery. The discharge appears to have been directly from the tanker as no evidence of crude is visible around the tank farm or valves. It was reported that AR trucking was the hauler and AR trucking did not report spill to either the operator or the Department. The crude traveled down a ditch line along Jamison Run Road for approximately 30 yds before it flowed through a culvert and continued another 60 yds into the forest. I performed a site visit on Monday July 7th. The impacted soil in the ditch lines was excavated and stock piled inside containment onsite. Several oil absorbent booms were placed in the ditch line to catch any residual crude that may flush out during a rain event. Future inspections will be conducted to evaluate if further remediation efforts will be required.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/03/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 105.46(a) - IMPLEMENTATION OF EROSION AND SEDIMENTATION CONTROL PLANS – During construction of water obstruction or encroachment, permittee failed to follow the erosion and sediment control plan prepared in accordance with Chapter 102 (relating to erosion and sediment control) and submitted as part of the application.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2026
Violation Code: 105.46(a) - IMPLEMENTATION OF EROSION AND SEDIMENTATION CONTROL PLANS – During construction of water obstruction or encroachment, permittee failed to follow the erosion and sediment control plan prepared in accordance with Chapter 102 (relating to erosion and sediment control) and submitted as part of the application.
Violation ID: 8284094
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/14/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Township, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/14/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8159090
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/14/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after a truck roll over caused produced fluid to be released along the access road on August 30, 2023. In an email sent to the Department by EQT representative Rick Hall on 9/5/23, he relayed that excavation was complete on the area impacted by the release along the access road. He said that the area of the impact had been delineated by environmental consultant Penn E and R using field instrumentation. He also stated that impacted material which had been excavated was staged within secondary containment on Pad A. Trees have been cleared from the area of the truck rollover on the west side of the access road as well as the area east of the NFG pipeline right-of-way at the north stormwater culvert. The full excavated area has been temporarily stabilized. No fluid was observed in the excavated area. Compost filter sock has been installed as appropriate around the excavated area. No E and S issues noted.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel was 1800 uS/cm. On Pad A, excavated material is tarped and sits within secondary containment. Six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment and they appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release on 2/21/23.

Comments: On 02/15/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received sample results from the 01/29/2025 collection date (Inspection Record No. 3907635). In reference to Inspection Record No. 3907635 pooled water off of the pad wide containment was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~ 19.99 mS/cm. There was a representative onsite at the time of the inspection. The DEP informed the representative of the elevated pooled water onsite and that samples were collected. The representative stated he would inform Steve Moyer and they would begin the clean up process. The DEP contacted Steve Moyer via phone call and left a message. The DEP spoke with representative Mike Deming at 1400 hours. He stated he was onsite. He stated equipment surrounding the area of elevated conductivity will be removed and the pooled water will be recovered to begin the clean up process.On 02/04/2025 representative Mike Deming informed the DEP that the AST equipment in the area of elevated pooled water was removed. Remediation of the impacted soils began that day and remediation will be continuing on 02/05/2025.The sample results are attached as a file. Comments: The site of this oil spill is in a forested area on an access road south off Center Hill Road, 430 yards on south branch of access. Will Warfel contacted WQS Taylor and reported to National Response Center that there was a release of about 20 gallons of crude oil from a tank the wind tipped over in one of the recent storms. The path of the crude oil was ~320 yards on the access from origin of the spill to low spot where it left the road and seeped into the stream. Blobs of oily material were found ~60 yards downstream. One absorbent boom was placed across the access road and one was positioned along the road to catch any remaining oil from seeping to stream. Visual clean-up of oil and oil contaminated soil completed where the tank tipped and leaked oil. The tank was removed and contaminated soil piled and covered until soil is tested and can be received at a licensed facility.Violations for the release of oil to ground and into a stream issued with this inspection. Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 4/24/2025
Comments: On April 24, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. According to the incident report that was submitted by the operator, this spill occurred on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM and resulted in an estimated 50 barrel release of production fluids to the ground. This spill report was received by the Department at 2:16 PM.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who explained that the brine tank valve failed and was ejected from the brine tank, which resulted in the release of an estimated 50 barrels of a brine and crude oil mixture. This was quantified based on the most recent fluid level measurement taken on the brine tank. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth are reported to have occurred. Penneco representative John Dohman was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Dohman who confirmed that no impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth have resulted from this incident. No identifiable water resources were visible from the location of the release. Mr. Dohman estimated that the release traveled approximately 70 yards down the slope adjacent to the brine tank and was stopped by a fallen tree. He explained that absorbent material was placed on the impacted area to absorb any standing production fluids and oil absorbent booms were placed downslope of the fallen tree that apparently stopped the release. Remediation of the impacted area is to be conducted by Moody and Associates and is scheduled to commence on the day following this inspection.The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). A gas odor was detected onsite during this inspection. An area of minor staining was observed on the surface of the well site (see photo 5). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 6). The failed brine tank valve appears to have been replaced (see photos 7 and 8). No fluids were observed escaping the brine tank at the time of inspection, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased. A path of brown staining was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank (see photos 9-18). The path of travel appears to be 70 yards, per Mr. Dohman's estimate. A faint crude oil odor was detectable from the impacted area. No evidence of visual impacts was observed downslope of the fallen tree that apparently stopped the travel of the released production fluids.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery. Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned. The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Seneca Resource's Dandois 482 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 5/3/2024 at 1100 hours. The weather was 70 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the DEP by Seneca Resources. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID # 380387 is tied to this release within CTS.Seneca Resource's reported to the DEP reporting hotline that on 5/2/2024 at ~2300 hours a produced water dump line washed out and caused a release of approximately 10 gallons of produced water to the pad surface (photos #1 and 2). The washout caused the produced water to be released in a concentrated spray which was stopped by a jersey barrier which is shown in photo #3. The jersey barrier prevented the release from being sprayed further across the pad. Seneca Resource's had a secondary containment structure and a roll-off waste container dispatched to the site for remedial activities. They planned to utilized a hydrovac truck (which was already onsite) to perform the majority of the clean-up around the pipes. A skid-steer was already utilized to scrape portions of the accessible areas. They planned to clean the jersey barrier prior to replacing it. A Seneca Resources representative onsite provided me with photos after remediation was completed (photos #4-6). The area has already been backfilled.Based on the reported release and Seneca Resource's timely remediation of the release, violations of the following are cited against API #117-20558 as immediately corrected at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)SWMA 301CSL 402(b)I departed the site at 1140 hours.

Violation Code: 78.66(e) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to take necessary corrective actions during release to prevent substance from reaching waters of this Commonwealth, recover or remove the released substance, and properly dispose of the substance in accordance with this subchapter or as approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8189877
Permit API: 125-23051
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: West Pike Run Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/03/2024
Comments: On 06/03/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the Zemba 1 well site following receipt of a spill report submitted by the operator on 05/31/2024 (CTS 381125). Penneco representatives on site. I called the operator on 06/03/2024 and they said that approximately 5 to 6 barrels were spilled on site and that the tank was cracked. The incident was discovered 05/31/2024 at 11:30 am and was reported to the Department on 05/31/2024 at 3:00 pm.Conductivity probe calibrated on 06/03/2024.The following was observed:The operator and well's information were posted on site, however the first three digits of the API were reading 126 instead of 125. I recommend that this is addressed. The tag on the well was displaying the last six digits of the API and not 125 (Photos 1, 2).Conductivity readings were taken at the site in the area that appeared to be impacted. A section of grass was dead and discolored near the tank (Photos 3-5). Readings were taken before and after calibration of the conductivity probe.Readings before calibration ranged from 25.4-852 uS/cm (Photos 6-9).Readings after calibration ranged from 227-1142 uS/cm (Photos 10-16).The tank was removed and additional readings were taken within the area with focus on the wet spots (Photos 17, 18). Readings were 20.5 uS/cm and 205 uS/cm (Photos 19, 20).The wellhead was in generally good condition with some corrosion (Photo 21).The Department requests the type of material released (brine or oil). The Department recommends that the Spill Policy is utilized due to a spill larger than 42 gallons. The Department also requests information on why the remediation was not started and/or the spill immediately addressed. Due to the observation of dead grass which is indicative of a fluid impact from the well site, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78.66(b), and 78.66(e) are being issued.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8201131
Permit API: 059-25626

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/11/2024
Comments: On 9/11/2024, I conducted a follow-up inspection of the Kentor Well Pad following violations issued on 9/9/2024 for a produced fluid spill proceeding the plugging of the Kentor 8H Well (Inspection ID: 3826729, Enforcement ID). Staining as a result of produced fluid spilling onto the Kentor Well Pad was discovered on 9/6/2024 following the removal of secondary containment used in the Kentor 8H Well plugging process. Leatherwood LLC was the Operator responsible for the spill, however EQT took responsibility for spill remediation. EQT is following Act 2 cleanup protocols as it is still unknown how much produced fluid was spilled.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI and Moody and Associates. I spoke to SPSI who confirmed that the spill had originated from the secondary containment during the Kentor 8H well plugging process, however it was still unclear how much produced fluid was spilled. A hole dug near the beginning of remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well yielded in produced fluid seeping into the hole. At the time of inspection, I observed produced fluid sitting within the excavated hole. SPSI stated that they were waiting for the arrival of Moody and Associates to proceed with remediation because the origin of the remaining produced fluid was unknown.While on site I observed the following:-Leatherwood LLC and EQTs Act 9 signs were posted at the site entrance (Photos 1-2).-Discoloration in the aggregate on site was apparent where excavation and impacted material remediation occurred (Photos 3-4).-The hole excavated by SPSI early in remediation was still seeping produced fluid at the time of inspection. It was undetermined where the produced fluid was seeping from and how much remained on site that was unaccounted for. I observed high conductivity of the fluid sitting in the hole (9.20 mS/cm), and the soil below the fluid was slightly elevated but below 3 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).-Previously stained aggregate located approximately 15 feet from the excavated hole demonstrated normal conductivity, and the top layer of aggregate appeared to be scraped off (Photo 12).-The plugged Kentor 8H well was barricaded by concrete barriers and backfilled since previous inspection. I observed normal conductivity readings in areas around the concrete barriers that were previously elevated (Photos 13-18).-Rolloff boxes were staged on site with impacted material. Boxes were being hauled off site at the time of inspection (Photo 19).-A ditch installed left of the plugged well was holding rainwater at the time of inspection (Photo 20).Because an unaccounted amount of produced fluid is still seeping from the Kentor Well Pad into the excavated hole approximately 75-100 feet from the origin of the spill, violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54 and SWMA 301 remain outstanding. Additionally, The Department is requesting a copy of the Kentor 8H well plugging secondary containment plan and all maintenance and inspection records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

Comments: On 2/4/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 10 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. Due to frozen conditions, conductivity readings were not taken during this inspection.When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows. Drilling to total depth has been completed on eight new gas wells at the site. Crews were on site, prepping for upcoming stimulation operations on the eight wells. Frac equipment was being mobilized to the location. Fracking has not commenced but is expected to start on 2/12/2026 depending on when the crew finishes on the DCNR 007 L Pad and depending on weather. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by the end of June 2026. In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Three sand separators remain near the wells but have been disconnected.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 0930 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/01/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8232157
Permit API: 125-28458
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Smith Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/01/2025
Comments: On May 1, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Malinky well pad in Smith Township, Washington County. According to the incident report that was submitted by Range Resources representative Nate Smiell, approximately 200 gallons of diethylene glycol was released to the surface of the well pad on the day of this inspection at 11:27 AM. No waterways are reported to have been impacted and remediation crew is on the way for cleanup. This spill report was submitted to the Department on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM. Mr. Smiell was present onsite for this inspection. Additional representatives from Range Resources and SPSI were also onsite conducting remediation.Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Smiell who further explained that diethylene glycol was being pumped from the GPU units in preparation for installation of secondary containment, per the requirements of an active Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) between the operator and the Department, when the pump truck operator erroneously pumped the diethylene glycol from the GPU into a chamber of the truck tank that was already full. This resulted in an estimated 200 gallons of diethylene glycol being released from a vent on the top of the truck's vessel and to the surface of well pad. Three spill cleanup drums were filled with absorbent material that soaked up the standing ethylene glycol on the well pad surface. Two rolloff boxes are expected to be required to contain the impacted material. Mr. Smiell then confirmed that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2. Mr. Smiell reported that at the time of this inspection, the majority of the impacted material appears to have been removed. This is based on testing that was conducted by Mr. Smiell throughout the impacted area, utilizing a glycol test kit, however a third-party environmental consultant is scheduled to take confirmation samples on the day following this inspection, per the requirements of Act 2. Excavation and remediation of the impacted area remains ongoing at the time of inspection (see photos 4-8, 12, and 17-19). The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Some minor potholes were observed in the access road (see photo 2). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 3). No Safety Data Sheet (SDS) was located onsite for diethylene glycol, the pollutant released during this incident. The GPU units are in the process of being equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 10). Well 2H is equipped with a well tag with no staining or evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be in production (see photos 14 and 15). Six additional wells are onsite that appear to be in production (see photo 13).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing pollutants to the surface of the ground and for failure to keep the SDS onsite for the pollutant released.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-03-19
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 845207
Permit API: 115-22162
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Apolacon Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-03-19
Comments: This administrative inspection report is created to document the Department's receipt of a Remediation Summary Report prepared by the Repsol subcontractor Resource Environmental of Montrose, PA. Kris Perritt, Environmental Specialist of Repsol submitted the report to the Department on 3/14/19. The report is in reference to a reported spill incident of (0.5) gallons of production fluid to the pad surface that was discovered on 2-14-19 at the site. The Department conducted an inspection at the site on 2-15-19. The Department and Resource recorded elevated (specific conductance) conductivity readings in the fluid spilled to the pad surface near the flowline of the 3H well. For additional details pertaining to the Department's 2-15-19 inspection report, refer to the 2-15-19 inspection report, efacts inspection ID# 2842245. The Remediation Summary Report contains the following information pertaining to the spill incident and remediation efforts. The location of the release was to snow and surficial pad material directly below a leaking union on the 3H flow line. The union was repaired, and visibly impacted snow and soil were hand shoveled into a (5) gallon bucket. The bucket was then staged in nearby secondary containment. Resource mobilized to the site as per the request of Repsol on 2/15/19 to conduct characterization and confirm remediation. Resource recorded elevated conductivity in a small depression created at the center of the excavation which measures (2) feet in width and (8) inches in length, and in soil screening locations within and around the excavation. Resource collected (2) confirmatory samples from the soil screening location within the excavation demonstrating the highest EC (electrical conductivity). The samples were sent to Test America Laboratories for analysis. Resource removed a small amount of soil from the bottom of the excavation, placed it into a container, and staged it on secondary containment. Resource used absorbents to empty the sump. Since 2/15/19, approximately (50) gallons of water have been removed from the sump, and electrical conductivity screenings have decreased below (1) millisienens/cm, ms/cm. The highest conductivity reading recorded by Resource was (6.6) ms/cm in water pooled in the excavation. Resource has concluded the spill has been visibly cleaned up, and laboratory results indicate remediation is complete. The spill volume has been revised from (0.5) gallons to (2) gallons. The Department conducted a review of the report on 3/19/19, and has concluded that no further action is warranted of Repsol at this time. Please forward the waste manifests to the Department of the material disposed of at a landfill upon receipt.
